Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
625 AM EST Sun Nov 1 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 152 AM EST Sunday...

Rainfall prospects for Tuesday are somewhat higher, and temperatures 
for Wednesday have been trended upwards to near record warmth in
the St. Lawrence Valley.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 152 AM EST Sunday...

1. Temperatures becoming warmer heading into November.

2. A cold front will move through the Northeast late this week 
bringing breezes and periods of rain possibly Thursday through the 
weekend.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 152 AM EST Sunday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: Little in the manner of impactful weather is expected 
over the next several days. High pressure will move offshore, and 
that will allow warm air to gradually filter into the region under 
steady south to southwest flow. This will bring 50s today, and then 
60s tomorrow. It'll still be on the dry side, but winds will 
generally be lighter where the lowest humidity values will be. 
Nighttime temperatures will also trend warmer, with only cooler 
hollows of sheltered valleys east of any mountain slopes below 
freezing tonight. There's still a tilted mid to upper level ridge 
that will be positioned to our west through about Tuesday. As it 
begins to translate eastwards, depending on the positioning of an 
upper vort, the surge of warm, moist advection could become 
collocated with marginal synoptic forcing. This would result in an 
area of clouds and light rain, mainly along the international border 
Tuesday into Tuesday night. Not every model scenario depicts rain, 
and so PoPs are mainly at or below 50 percent at this time.

Once the upper ridge is offshore, temperatures will climb into the 
mid 60s to lower 70s for Wednesday in response to somewhat tighter 
pressure gradients as a surface low tracks over far northern Quebec 
Province. A few daily record highs may be in striking distance. 
Ushering in the warmth will be south winds gusting around 15-25 mph 
with localized observations around 30 mph, especially in the broader 
valleys.

KEY MESSAGE 2: Model consensus favors a full meridional trough ejecting 
out of the Plains Wednesday night with a cold front passing 
through the Northeast between Thursday and Friday. Timing spread
has narrowed a little, but model discrepancies remain on how 
fast the high pressure shifts eastward, the timing of the front 
itself, and the strength of frontal dynamics. Some models are 
stalling the boundary in the vicinity of Vermont streaming ample
moisture across the region while others are more progressive 
with flow resulting in more distinct rounds of rainfall. While 
the details are sparse, most guidance agrees that there is a 
good shot at an extended period of rain chances with the 
trailing upper low becoming at least partially cut off. This 
would promote lingering shower chances through the weekend 
potentially into early next week. The details that are more 
predictable are continued warm temperatures under southerly flow
Thursday with some southerly breezes ongoing as well. Beyond 
Thursday, temperatures are favored to cool back towards seasonal
averages with coldest air locked well north of the region.

&&

.AVIATION /12Z SUNDAY THROUGH THURSDAY/...
Through 12Z Monday...VFR conditions are expected to continue 
through the forecast period except for  SLK through 14Z due to 
freezing fog and stratus. This will lift and scatter after
sunrise, but may take a little longer given the decreasing sun
angle. Otherwise, southerly flow picks up this afternoon with 
some gusts to around 20kts at MSS and PBG with 12-18kts more 
likely at other terminals. High clouds increase overnight and
begin to lower heading into Monday. 

Outlook...

Monday: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Monday Night: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Tuesday: VFR. Chance SHRA.
Tuesday Night: VFR. Chance SHRA.
Wednesday: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Wednesday Night: VFR. Chance RA.
Thursday: VFR. Chance RA.

&&

.CLIMATE...
Temperatures could approach record highs on November 4th with
the greatest chance at KMSS.

Record    | Forecast
71 (2022) | 71

&&

.BTV WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
VT...None.
NY...None.

&&
